name: Obil
title: Overseer of the camels
summary: Obil was an Ishmaelite who served under King David as the overseer of the camels in the king's service. He is mentioned only once in the Bible, in 1 Chronicles 27:30, as part of the list of David's officials and administrators. His role shows that David's kingdom was well organized with specialized administrators over the king's property.

keyEvents.title: Overseer of David's camels
keyEvents.description: Obil, an Ishmaelite, was appointed to be in charge of King David's camels as part of the royal administration.

keyEvents.title: Part of David's administrative system
keyEvents.description: Obil is mentioned among several officials who managed King David's property, including cattle, donkeys, sheep, and other resources.

keyEvents.title: An Ishmaelite in David's service
keyEvents.description: Obil's background as an Ishmaelite shows that David included people from various ethnic groups in his administration, which testifies to the diversity of the kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Management of royal resources
keyEvents.description: Camels were important transport and trade animals in the ancient Middle East, and Obil's role was crucial for the king's logistics and trade.
